The same as `no-inner-declarations`, but a declaration at the top level of a `<script>` of a component is at the root. With the defaults it reports nothing in a component or a module: they are strict mode, where a function in a block belongs to the block.

On a file that is no component it is the core rule.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/no-inner-declarations": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"options": ["functions", {"blockScopedFunctions": "disallow"}]} */}

```svelte
<script>
  if (user) {
    function greet() {}
  }
</script>
```

{/* bad {"options": ["both"]} */}

```svelte
<script>
  if (user) {
    var name = user.name;
  }
</script>
```

Not reported, a function at the top level of the script:

{/* good {"options": ["both", {"blockScopedFunctions": "disallow"}]} */}

```svelte
<script>
  function greet() {}
  let name;
  if (user) {
    name = user.name;
    greet();
  }
</script>
```

## Options

The first option says what to look at:

| Option                  | What it does                                     |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `"functions"` (default) | Report `function` declarations in nested blocks  |
| `"both"`                | Also report `var` declarations in nested blocks  |

| Option                 | Default   | What it does                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `blockScopedFunctions` | `"allow"` | `"allow"`: a function in a block in strict mode is not reported. `"disallow"`: it is reported |
